amd_gpu_decision.reason: The current scientific question is NVIDIA RT cores versus Embree CPU cores. Adding AMD now would widen the matrix before the NVIDIA-vs-CPU story is publication-clean.
amd_gpu_decision.recommended_timing: Prepare AMD GPU only after v2.13 has an accepted RayJoin authors-code comparison, a PIP optimization/explanation packet, and a public wording packet with zero unexplained rows.

contact_manifold.readout: reasonable tiny-row Embree win; needs human-scale batching

rtnn.readout: near-parity backend row; not an RT-core neighbor-search claim

lsi.readout: strong RT-core value row and RTDL OptiX faster than RayJoin RT for scalar count

pip.readout: clear OptiX-over-Embree improvement, but current RTDL optimization debt versus RayJoin RT

row_review.analysis: Moderate OptiX win is credible because this row is a native node-coverage threshold decision, not Barnes-Hut force integration.
row_review.v2_13_action: Keep the force-vector and paper-reproduction boundary visible.

row_review.analysis: Embree winning is credible for this tiny bounded collect-k witness row; launch and orchestration overhead can dominate the RT path.
row_review.v2_13_action: Add a human-scale repeated batch before any public wording.

row_review.analysis: The OptiX win is plausible for a prepared threshold count where traversal dominates more than output materialization.
row_review.v2_13_action: Keep exact-distance and whole-app claims blocked.

row_review.analysis: Large OptiX win is credible after the native Embree AABB route replaced the old columnar fallback; this is a prepared query median.
row_review.v2_13_action: Scale box/query counts and report prepare amortization separately.

row_review.analysis: Large OptiX win is credible for a prepared ray/triangle grouped count; the row is not SQL, DBMS, or typed stream timing.
row_review.v2_13_action: Keep DB wording blocked and add typed hit-stream evidence separately.

row_review.analysis: Small tail-total OptiX win is credible because the compact-flag contract is already tiny; traversal wins are partly hidden by fixed overhead.
row_review.v2_13_action: Report native traversal and tail-total side by side.

row_review.analysis: Large OptiX win is credible because both rows hold the same Numba continuation fixed and differ mainly in the RTDL geometric prefilter.
row_review.v2_13_action: Preserve the partner-fixed route and avoid whole-app DBSCAN wording.

row_review.analysis: Near parity is credible and is not an RT-core neighbor-search claim because the current OptiX row is a prepared ranked-summary route.
row_review.v2_13_action: Either build a true RT-core neighbor-search row or keep this as backend-only.

row_review.analysis: Strong OptiX win is credible: same RayJoin-exported stream, scalar count, exact count match, and no RTDL row materialization.
row_review.row_label: Spatial RayJoin LSI same-stream scalar count
row_review.v2_13_action: Retain in the Goal4367 authors-code packet with stream hashes.

row_review.analysis: Near parity against Embree and slower-than-RayJoin RT are credible because exact membership refinement and generic front-door overhead dominate the current row.
row_review.row_label: Spatial RayJoin PIP same-stream scalar count
row_review.v2_13_action: Use Goal4368 as the improved exact baseline, then keep attacking exact refinement.

row_review.analysis: Large OptiX win is credible for a prepared ray/triangle any-hit count; this is query/count timing rather than whole application time.
row_review.v2_13_action: Keep prepared-query wording and add larger human-scale repeats.

acceptance_gate: Do not move the v2.12 tag without explicit maintainer decision.
All v2.13 wording must distinguish baseline evidence from new claims.
roadmap_goals.deliverable: A stable v2.12 source-tree tag and comparison packet used only as baseline evidence.
roadmap_goals.title: Freeze v2.12 as the bounded release baseline

acceptance_gate: Same exported query stream schema and hashes are reported.
RayJoin Query ms, build/index ms, and RTDL hot query ms are separate columns.
Each speedup column states which direction is good.
LSI and PIP each have a reasonability paragraph tied to measured phases.
roadmap_goals.deliverable: A table covering RayJoin grid, LBVH, and RT logs versus RTDL OptiX and RTDL Embree for LSI and PIP scalar-count contracts.
roadmap_goals.title: Compare against RayJoin authors code on the same streams

acceptance_gate: Candidate generation, download, exact refinement, and Python/front-door timing are visible.
The row is rejected for public speedup wording unless the observed speedup has a phase-level explanation.
A successful optimization keeps the exact prepared-points count contract and count agreement.
roadmap_goals.deliverable: A measured PIP packet that either closes the gap to RayJoin RT or proves why the exact RTDL contract remains dominated by refinement.
roadmap_goals.title: Turn Spatial RayJoin PIP from explanation debt into optimization evidence

acceptance_gate: Every compared Embree row uses a native route or explicitly names the partner continuation.
Thread/environment settings are included in each run packet.
Fallback and boundary-limited rows are excluded from release-facing speedups.
roadmap_goals.deliverable: A repeatable Embree CPU protocol with thread counts, warmups, repeats, native traversal time, and fallback detection for every promoted row.
roadmap_goals.title: Harden the Embree CPU side as the serious multicore baseline

acceptance_gate: Batching is repeat-only and does not smuggle in unrelated setup work.
Per-query and aggregate timing are both reported.
Contact Manifold, Robot Collision, LibRTS, and triangle-counting tiny rows are included first.
roadmap_goals.deliverable: A timing packet that reports 1-10 second aggregate batches plus per-query medians for sub-ms rows.
roadmap_goals.title: Make tiny rows human-scale without changing the contract

acceptance_gate: No broad RT-core speedup wording.
No whole-application speedup wording unless end-to-end evidence exists.
No RTDL-beats-RayJoin wording except for exact rows where the authors-code comparison supports it.
Every surprising row has a written explanation or is marked not publishable.
roadmap_goals.deliverable: A publication table where every speedup has a same-contract basis, a direction definition, and an observed-speedup explanation.
roadmap_goals.title: Produce the public comparison wording only after row-level explanations pass

acceptance_gate: RayJoin authors-code comparison packet is complete.
PIP either improves or has a phase-level explanation accepted for public wording.
The public wording packet passes with zero unexplained speedup rows.
roadmap_goals.deliverable: A go/no-go decision for AMD after v2.13 credibility gates pass.
roadmap_goals.title: Defer AMD GPU work until the NVIDIA-vs-Embree story is credible
